title: Cleaning a messy CSV
summary: Real-world input: stray whitespace, a byte-order mark, blank lines, money strings, bad values and duplicates, with line-numbered error reports.
hints: `parse_amount`: `cleaned = text.strip().replace("$", "").replace(",", "")`, raise `ValueError` if `cleaned` is empty, and otherwise `return float(cleaned)` (which raises `ValueError` itself for junk). Round to 2 decimals with `round(value, 2)`.

Open with `encoding="utf-8-sig"` so a leading byte-order mark disappears from the first header. Read rows with `csv.reader` and loop `for line_no, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):` (the header is line 1). Skip rows where every field is blank: `if not any(field.strip() for field in row): continue`. Note: for this exercise there are no quoted line breaks, so row numbers and line numbers agree.

For each row: strip every field and zip it with the stripped headers into a dict. Check in this order: `len(row) != len(header)` -> `"line N: expected 3 fields, got 4"`; missing `customer` -> `"line N: missing customer"`; amount that `parse_amount` rejects -> `"line N: bad amount 'xyz'"` (use the stripped original text with `!r`); an `order_id` already seen -> `"line N: duplicate order_id 7"`. Otherwise title-case the customer, store the float amount and remember the id in a set.
